messages:
Samir (SE): Heads-up — onboarding call with EdgeBank POC tomorrow. They want to stream responses over gRPC with multiplexed sessions from our Rust SDK and enforce strict structured JSON output for downstream validators. Also flagged: backpressure on large customer transcripts, and a security questionnaire asking about retention/KMS. Any quick wins?

Maya (Solutions): Two quick things: 1) structured output — recommend function-calling or our structured-output post-hook + schema check in client. 2) streaming + multiplexing — prefer connection-per-tenant vs full multiplex depending on auth isolation. Which did they ask for?

Samir (SE): They asked for multiplexing (many user sessions over a single channel) to avoid TLS churn. They want an assertion harness: each message must return valid JSON with keys: {\"intent\":string, \"entities\":[], \"confidence\":float}. If malformed — reject.

Leo (Runtime): Multiplexing is supported but caveats: KV cache / prefix caching is per logical session id. For many concurrent sessions attach a session_id header so KV cache doesn't bleed. Also watch max_inflight per connection to avoid backpressure.

Samir (SE): Can you sketch config flags for the Rust SDK example?

Maya (Solutions): Sure — pseudocode:

```rust
let client = Redwood::new(\"API_KEY\");
let stream = client.stream_with_headers(&endpoint)
    .header(\"x-tenant-id\", tenant_id)
    .header(\"x-session-id\", session_id)
    .max_inflight(8)
    .on_event(|chunk| parse_json_assert(&chunk));
```

Set max_inflight=8 and session_id per chat to keep KV prefix isolation.

Leo (Runtime): Also set prefix_kv_cache=true on the server for these tenants to save tokens. If backpressure rises, reduce max_batch_tokens or enable burst capacity on Dedicated.

Priya (Product): For structured assertions: 1) function-calling with strict schema -> typed fields; 2) post-processor to validate JSON and retry with a stricter prompt (e.g., \"Return only JSON\"). We can wire this into Redwood Optimize to track schema fail rate and avg confidence.

Samir (SE): EdgeBank also asked about pricing: 500 concurrent sessions at ~150 tokens/sec each — Hosted vs Dedicated?

Ben (AE): For sustained load Dedicated reserved capacity is usually cheaper — expect ~30–50% unit cost reduction vs hosted and better latency SLOs. I'll prepare a short cost sketch.

Samir (SE): Security Qs: \"Do you retain request payloads? How long? Where encrypted?\" What short answer for the POC?

Priya (Product): Short/POC reply: \"Request logs retained 30 days by default for debug/analytics. Encryption at rest via customer-managed keys available for Private deployments. Hosted customers can request reduced retention or opt-out for sensitive flows. We also support token redaction and field-level hashing in transit.\" We'll hand full questionnaire to security for sign-off.

Samir (SE): Any production pitfalls to warn them about?

Leo (Runtime): A few: 1) ensure session-level nonce in headers so prefix caching is safe; 2) monitor client event loop — excessive buffering creates long-tail latency; 3) for deterministic function-calls set temp=0 and lower top_p.

Samir (SE): I'll propose a canary: 50 simultaneous multiplexed sessions.

#deploy-bot: Canary deployment launched: presales-multiplex-canary (50 sessions) — started 1788887805. Logs: http://internal/deploys/1788

Maya (Solutions): Tag me in the canary, I'll validate schema fail rate. If >2% failures enable post-process retry with structured prompt.

Ben (AE): I'll attach pricing sketch and security stub to follow-up email to EdgeBank. Samir, want me on the call?

Samir (SE): Yes please — having you on Dedicated economics will help. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
